reproduction_manifest.notes: AUDC=0.7225 reproduced within CI [0.72,0.80] using KNN predictors (k=128) on RouterArena data (8400 queries, Qwen3-0.6B embeddings, 16 models). QNC=0.5427 and Peak Acc=0.7432 are outside paper CI bounds due to different model pool (RouterArena vs R2-BENCH) and predictor architecture (KNN vs 3-layer MLP). 5 independent runs with different seeds. The paper's default embedding is Qwen3-0.6B; MiniLM-L6-v2 (384d) is used only in Table 2 ablation. The public repo ships with online routing code (Ridge+Qwen3-0.6B) and RouterArena evaluation scripts; the paper's experiment code for MiniLM-L6-v2 + MLP training is not in the public repo.
reproduction_manifest.eval_output_format: stdout prints Peak Accuracy, AUDC (norm cost), QNC; also saved to --output-dir/metrics.json with keys peak_accuracy, AUDC, QNC
reproduction_manifest.known_levers: KNN neighbors (k: 16-256), train fraction (0.5-0.9), cost normalization method, model pool subset selection, embedding standardization. Moving to MLP predictor (paper architecture: 3-layer [256,128,64], Adam lr=1e-4, 100 epochs, MSE) may improve results but requires fixing the training data/model pool mismatch.
reproduction_manifest.setup_notes: Container was started from docker.1ms.run/pytorch/pytorch:2.1.0-cuda12.1-cudnn8-runtime (manual fallback image). Dependencies installed: scikit-learn==1.7.2, pandas, matplotlib, joblib, sentence-transformers, huggingface_hub, tqdm. numpy downgraded to 1.26.4 for PyTorch 2.1.0 compatibility. RouterArena training data downloaded from huggingface.co/datasets/JiaqiXue/R2-Bench-RouterArena to /datasets/: training_data.pkl (40MB), routerarena_embeddings.pkl (34MB), router_data_10.json (860KB). The training_data.pkl contains Qwen3-0.6B embeddings (8400 queries, 1024d) with per-model per-budget accuracy and token counts for 16 LLMs. The repo's r2_router/checkpoints/ contain pre-trained Ridge regression checkpoints for 11 R2-BENCH models but were NOT used here because they target a different model pool. The evaluation script (run_eval_v2.py) is self-contained and uses sklearn KNeighborsRegressor with cosine distance and distance-weighted averaging.

optimization_objective.summary: Improve AUDC (higher=better overall quality-cost tradeoff) while monitoring QNC (lower=better cost at quality target) and Peak Acc (higher=better maximum quality). QNC and Peak Acc are antagonistic per the rubric — improving cost-efficiency may reduce peak quality and vice versa.

metrics.name: AUDC
metrics.rationale: Area Under Deferral Curve measures the overall quality-cost tradeoff. This is the primary summary metric for routing performance. Paper reports 0.76 with MiniLM-L6-v2 + MLP on R2-BENCH.

metrics.name: QNC
metrics.rationale: Query-Normalized Cost measures the minimum relative cost to match the best single LLM's quality. Lower is better. Antagonistic with Peak Acc — reducing QNC may reduce peak accuracy. Paper reports 0.32.

metrics.name: Peak Acc.
metrics.rationale: Peak Accuracy is the maximum quality achieved by the routing system. Antagonistic with QNC — pursuing peak accuracy alone may increase cost. Paper reports 0.79.

optimization_objective.success_policy: Primary goal: maximize AUDC. Accept QNC and Peak Acc changes as long as AUDC improves and neither guardrail degrades beyond its regression tolerance. If AUDC improves but a guardrail regresses beyond tolerance, the improvement is valid only if the Pareto frontier shows net gain.
